transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Head of Platform, Northfield), Marta Ruiz (Security Lead, Northfield), Steve O'Connor (VP Eng, Northfield)
Links shared: Redwood Trust Center deck: https://app.redwood.ai/trustcenter-demo (shared in chat), control-mapping template: (drive link)
Summary: Quick posture review focused on SOC 2 / ISO 27001 coverage, onboarding to Redwood Trust Center, RBAC/SSO integration points (Okta/SCIM), audit logs access and KMS/HSM encryption key flow. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated but security gating is primary.
Topics: scope of SOC 2 & ISO artifacts, Trust Portal access model, evidence mapping process, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log retention and streaming, KMS/HSM integration and key custody, data residency (EU), timeline for evidence handoff.
Action items: see metadata.
Questions: what evidence will be available in Trust Center? how is key lifecycle managed for private deployments? who is control owner mapping?

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect in places):
[00:00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for carving time today, um we wanted to run through the posture and Trust Portal access so you can see where the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts live and map to your controls.
[00:00:18] Jordan: cool yeah thanks Alex. Quick intro — i'm Jordan, we own platform at Northfield. Marta's in security and Steve's on for oversight.
[00:00:30] Marta: hi thanks. main thing for us is audit evidence pathing, data residency, and how keys are handled if we go private.
[00:00:38] Priya: great, we'll cover both hosted and private flows. One note, our "Trust Center" sometimes shows up as TrustPortal in older docs — apologies for the naming flip, it's the same place.
[00:00:52] Steve: good to know. timeline wise we're aiming for an internal audit window mid-november, so we need the mapping and reports before then.
[00:01:05] Alex: got it. we'll aim to drop the SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO scope doc into the portal by friday. Also we'll send the control mapping template.
[00:01:18] Jordan: on the SOC 2, is that the full Type II with the auditor opinion and system description?
[00:01:26] Alex: yes, full Type II with the opinion and the system description. sometimes the transcriber munges the word "system" — but you'll get the standard AICPA format plus our control narrative.
[00:01:38] Marta: will the Trust Center have historic log samples? like auditor friendly extracts or just policy docs?
[00:01:46] Priya: we surface three classes: policies and reports (SOC/ISO PDFs), exported evidence bundles (for controls) and a limited set of anonymized audit log samples for sample-level review. full raw logs are not exposed in the portal for hosted customers but we can stream logs to your SIEM or provide S3 exports via a dedicated arrangement.
[00:02:05] Jordan: ok, we use Splunk — can you stream?
[00:02:09] Priya: yes, we have a log-streaming connector for Splunk and S3. for SSO we also capture auth events to the audit stream.
[00:02:18] Steve: important: data residency — our EU customers data needs to stay in eu-1 region, is that supported?
[00:02:26] Alex: yes, region pinning supported in both Hosted and Dedicated. for Private we run inside your VPC and data never leaves your network unless you configure cross-region replication.
[00:02:38] Marta: about KMS, are you using customer-managed keys (CMK) or do we have to hand keys over? what's the HSM story?
[00:02:45] Priya: good question. we support two patterns: 1) hosted w/ Redwood-managed envelope keys (we manage KMS/HSM on our side) and 2) BYOK for Dedicated/Private where you can bring a key from your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) or a hardware HSM via Cloud HSM or an on-prem HSM. when BYOK is used, Redwood stores only encrypted key material and we call your KMS for unwrap operations. we'll show a diagram in the KMS deep dive.
[00:03:12] Jordan: does bringing a key change SOC coverage?
[00:03:16] Alex: audit scope doesn't change — but control evidence differs; with BYOK you provide evidence of your KMS configuration and key rotation logs; we include call traces showing key unwraps as part of the audit evidence bundle.
[00:03:30] Marta: rotation cadence — do you enforce rotation or is it on customer side?
[00:03:34] Priya: rotation is on your side for BYOK; for Redwood-managed keys we rotate per our key policy and provide rotation logs. we'll include the policy in the Trust Center.
[00:03:44] Steve: on RBAC and SSO: we use Okta with SCIM provisioning. can we map roles to Redwood routes and restrict model access per-team?
[00:03:53] Alex: yep. we support SAML/SSO (Okta, Azure AD), SCIM for user provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. you can set per-route/model ACLs and audit who called which model and with which token.
[00:04:08] Jordan: any pitfalls with SCIM attributes? we saw some mismatch in group names in another vendor.
[00:04:13] Priya: we recommend syncing 'groups' and using a group-to-role mapping; we'll share our SCIM attribute guide. common gotcha is email vs username mismatches.
[00:04:22] Marta: for evidence mapping, how do you present control ownership? do you expect us to map control owners to Redwood docs?
[00:04:29] Alex: yes we provide a template where each control maps to one or more evidence artifacts in the portal and you can assign owner names. for example, control CC6 maps to key rotation logs (owner: Marta) and deployment config (owner: Jordan).
[00:04:44] Steve: can we run a quick walk through of the Trust Center UI?
[00:04:47] Alex: sure i can share my screen — (screen share started) — top left is Reports & Attestations, then Evidence Bundles, then Admin settings where you can invite external auditors.
[00:05:05] [screen noises] Alex: here's the SOC 2 pdf thumbnail, ISO certificate, and the Evidence tab where you can filter by control id.
[00:05:20] Jordan: looks good. what's the access model for auditors — do we grant them read-only portal access?
[00:05:25] Priya: yes read-only time-limited invites, with optional NDA gating. we can generate an auditor link that expires after X days and records auditor activity in the audit log.
[00:05:36] Marta: do you capture auditor downloads in the audit logs?
[00:05:39] Priya: yes, download events are recorded with timestamp and user identity; those are part of the audit log stream.
[00:05:45] Jordan: we need to map the ISO Annex A controls too — is that a separate artifact?
[00:05:50] Alex: we include ISO 27001 mapping in the portal for customers who've asked; it's a mapping doc that links ISO Annex A to Redwood controls and sample evidence. we'll upload an annotated mapping in the control template.
[00:06:03] Steve: when you say sample evidence bundles — what's the granularity? like per-control or per-scope system?
[00:06:09] Priya: per-control + per-system. you can download a zip for each control that includes the required artifacts (config exports, logs, screenshots, policy snippets).
[00:06:18] Jordan: about the logs — retention and tamper evidence? we need immutable retention for certain log classes.
[00:06:24] Priya: we support WORM-like retention policies via S3 object lock if you want immutable retention; audit logs include cryptographic checksums and we can publish digest snapshots for tamper detection.
[00:06:36] Marta: excellent. on the evidence handoff process, do you expect us to upload anything into the Trust Center or is Redwood the source of truth?
[00:06:44] Alex: it's hybrid. Redwood populates system-generated evidence; customers can upload their own evidence for downstream controls (e.g., vendor attestations, internal policy docs). the control mapping template indicates whether evidence is customer-supplied or Redwood-supplied.
[00:06:59] Jordan: ok. are there document classification tags so we can mark PII or restricted assets?
[00:07:04] Priya: yes you can tag evidence with classification labels, and RBAC can restrict viewing to specific groups.
[00:07:12] Steve: any limitations for private on-prem deployments? specifically, will the Trust Center still be able to index evidence if deployed air-gapped?
[00:07:20] Alex: for air-gapped/private we ship a connector that you run inside your network which pushes metadata and evidence bundles to a customer-specific Trust Portal endpoint; if fully air-gapped, we can provide an on-prem Trust Center instance under a separate enterprise contract.
[00:07:38] Marta: what's the lead time for on-prem Trust Center?
[00:07:41] Priya: typically 6–8 weeks for installation + validation. most customers use the hosted Trust Portal with dedicated VPC peering to avoid that timeline.
[00:07:52] Jordan: okay that helps our planning.
[00:07:58] [00:08:00] Alex: quick note on controls mapping: we'll send a spreadsheet where each Redwood control has columns for 'evidence type', 'artifact link', 'owner', and 'notes'. please fill owner and mark anything that is blocked.
[00:08:16] Jordan: sounds good.
[00:08:20] Marta: about encryption in transit — we need TLS details and cipher suites for the assessor.
[00:08:25] Priya: TLS 1.2/1.3 with modern ciphers, we provide cipher list and cert rotation cadence in the network security section of the SOC report.
[00:08:33] Steve: is mutual TLS supported for service-to-service?
[00:08:36] Priya: mTLS supported for private endpoints; we'll document the handshake and cert management process.
[00:08:43] Jordan: what about model data retention? we have to ensure prompt data isn't kept beyond X days in eu-1.
[00:08:49] Alex: you can configure retention windows per-tenant; default is 30 days for user-level traces but we can set to shorter or zero retention for ephemeral workloads. retention settings are surfaced in the Admin panel and are part of the evidence set.
[00:09:02] Marta: any differences in retention behavior between hosted and dedicated?
[00:09:06] Priya: dedicated gives you stronger guarantees around retention and physical isolation; hosted still respects retention but the underlying infra is shared. we'll outline the specific SLAs in the contract.
[00:09:18] Steve: competitors question — a few of our folks asked how Redwood differs from OtherCloudAI on trust docs — any short nuggets?
[00:09:26] Alex: main differentiators are production-focused observability (per-route cost & latency traces) and the Trust Center that bundles curated evidence + streaming connectors. we can send a short comparison doc after.
[00:09:41] Jordan: great. next, can we talk about evidence format for control A.7? (role assignment)
[00:09:46] Priya: for role assignment we usually show SCIM audit logs, provisioning events, and a snapshot export of the RBAC matrix from the Console. that satisfies many auditors.
[00:09:57] Marta: about SCIM — do you provision groups automatically or is it just users?
[00:10:02] Priya: we support groups + nested groups in Okta; we map group names to roles in the Console. the provisioning logs show timestamps and actor.
[00:10:12] Steve: any sample of the provisioning log we can see?
[00:10:15] Alex: yes we'll attach a redacted sample in the control mapping spreadsheet.
[00:10:20] Jordan: i'd like to schedule the KMS deep dive with Priya — week of Oct 6 works for us.
[00:10:25] Priya: i'm available; i'll send calendar options.
[00:10:30] Marta: two quick audit questions: 1) how are change management evidence artifacts captured? 2) is build provenance stored?
[00:10:37] Priya: change management — we snapshot deployment manifests and include deployment audit events (git commit id + deploy author). build provenance depends on your CI; we can ingest SBOMs and store them as artifacts linked to deployment controls.
[00:10:50] Steve: very helpful.
[00:10:54] Alex: i'm going to recap — i'll upload SOC2 and ISO artifacts, send the mapping template, invite you to the Trust Center with read-only rights, and Priya will own the KMS deep dive scheduling. Marta and Jordan will provide RBAC and scoped-system lists.
[00:11:12] Jordan: correct. one more thing — what's the expected size of evidence bundles? we have some heavy logs and we don't want to overload the portal.
[00:11:20] Priya: evidence bundles are zipped and we support large file upload to S3-backed storage; portal will show pointers and you can opt to keep large artifacts in your S3 and link to them.
[00:11:33] Marta: ok that works.
[00:11:36] Steve: do you have a recommended naming convention for uploaded artifacts to make auditor searches easier?
[00:11:41] Alex: we recommend <control>-<artifact-type>-<date>-<owner>.pdf. we'll include a naming guidance doc in the template.
[00:11:51] [00:12:00] Alex: any final questions from the team?
[00:12:04] Jordan: not right now. thanks for the clear run-through.
[00:12:07] Marta: thanks — please get that invite link by friday.
[00:12:11] Steve: thanks all.
[00:12:15] Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in chat with the assets and schedule.
[00:12:20] [call moves to next topics and scheduling logistics; remainder of call used for calendar pegging and brief technical clarifications not transcribed verbatim]
[00:54:30] Alex: final note — if you hit a blocker when mapping controls ping our security PD. we'll also open a support ticket and link it to your CRM.
[00:54:42] Jordan: thanks, see you all in the deep dive.

End of transcript.
